offlineSyntheticCheck.reason: The FB-count check and the page/mapping checks live in VerifierHSafetyPLC/VerifierEL6910 and PublisherEL6910. They need a SafetyProjectNode (VS hierarchy/ErrorListHandler, alias-device directory, ApplicationLanguageHandler). The SDK DLLs expose no headless verifier entry point. The only offline route is IDE 'Verify Safety Project' in TcXaeShell (no target needed). That was not started here: it is outside this read-only slice, and IDE results must stay separate
offlineSyntheticCheck.proposedProcedure: Isolated copy of the solution (no target connection): add dummy FBAnd blocks in TwinSafeGroup1 until AllFunctionBlocks = 512, run Verify -> expect no MaxFunctionBlockNumber error; add one more (513) -> expect 'Too many function blocks configured for chosen target system EL1918 (maximum number of 512 allowed).' Also record whether 'Too many functionblocks, connections or groups have been added for the selected target system.' (pages) appears earlier, and at which count

risks: R1 page budget: 12 x 2048-byte safe-logic pages can be exhausted before 512 FBs. The FB count at which this happens is NV. It is the most likely real limit for a large AND/OR-heavy graph

R2 editor vs firmware: the editor takes the limit from ESI/SDK. The firmware (V01.08) has its own download-time checks ('The received number of FBs (%d) was too big, the maximum allowed value is %d', ESI diag text). The firmware value is not exposed offline (NV). ESI and the public docs both say 512

R3 default fallback: if TargetSystemSubType is ever empty or missing (for example after a regenerated TargetSystemConfig.xml during V14-Q2 hardware-config work), the editor selects EL6900 -> 255 FBs / 32 groups / 2912-byte process image
R4 revision: a replacement EL1918 with RevisionNo #x00110000 has a different ESI block (process image 20224, TwinSAFE SC master 128). FB/group/connection limits are unchanged
R5 counting: the limit is per target across all groups. User-FB instances count as their internal FBs
R6 cycle time grows with project size (EL6910 doc ~1 ms depending on project size). This is not a hard limit, but it affects FSoE watchdogs. Not assessed (out of scope; timers are not changed)
